name: Thompson Washington D.C.
positioning: Thompson hotel in Washington D.C.'s Navy Yard, near Nationals Park and the Anacostia waterfront, with nautical design touches and a rooftop bar
best_for: Baseball fans heading to Nationals Park
Travelers who want a waterfront neighborhood base with a rooftop bar

facts.text: The hotel is at 221 Tingey Street SE in Washington, D.C.'s Navy Yard neighborhood.
The nearest Metro station is Navy Yard-Ballpark on the Green Line.
Conde Nast Traveler says the hotel is steps from the Nationals baseball stadium and right by the Anacostia waterfront and marina.
The design includes subtle nods to the Navy Yard's nautical history in public spaces and guest rooms.
New York-based Parts and Labor Design did the interiors.
The Thompson Bar Room serves light bites, wine and handcrafted cocktails.
The rooftop bar has floor-to-ceiling windows and terrace seating.
Some suites and guest rooms have a private balcony.
Rooms have D.S. & Durga bath amenities.
The rooftop lounge has over 6,000 square feet of bookable event space.
Dogs are welcome at no additional charge for stays under 30 nights.
The hotel suggests a bike ride along the Anacostia Riverwalk Trail.

highlights.text: The Rooftop at the Thompson offers 360-degree views of Washington D.C. and the waterfront.
Curved walls, porthole-style lights and mirrored accents link to the neighborhood's history as a naval center.
The Thompson Suite Ballpark View looks onto the national ballpark through floor-to-ceiling windows and has a balcony.
The 1 King River View room looks out on the Anacostia River.
The daily destination fee includes access to pedal assist electric bicycles and a Capital Bikeshare day pass.

considerations.text: A daily destination fee applies to each room.
Parking is by valet, which includes in-and-out privileges.
WhataHotel notes an urban location with typical city noise levels.

sources.title: Conde Nast Traveler: Thompson Washington D.C. review
